doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Being overlooked and Europe with Wim Wigt
summary: He feels overlooked by writers while Europe sold out, and Wim Wigt booked him and made The Forgotten Man.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Do you feel that you’ve been somewhat overlooked by people who write about the
Not really... Oh yeah. By the people who write. Yeah, of course. Of course. Of course. I told you I just went to Europe, and every place was sold out.
Now, when did you start going to Europe regularly?
Is it different playing for a European audience than let’s say an inner city...
Do you do the same thing, or do you take a different presentation?
I play the same thing. Same thing. Same thing. This guy Wim Wigt started booking me.
Hence, you started recording for Timeless and other...

Timeless, yeah. He even made an album called The Forgotten Man. He said, “People forgot about you.” I said, “they didn’t really forget about me, because I started working, and I wasn’t in town.” I was working like on the road. And the jazz critics, people, they don’t get around that much. Cut that off for a minute.
